svg.text: Preliminary tenant-admin account; root cause and fleet figures are not publicly audited.

g.text: 1. Reported Cause & SKU Divergence
Preliminary
July 2026 Gateway Update
Connection-handling logic updated in internal
Windows gateway services fronting Exchange.
Under critical load, coarse synchronization locks
created severe thread convoying and backoff stalls.
Reportedly latent across fleet for over three months.
Staging vs. Production Divergence
Lab testing ran on smaller VM SKUs (8-16 cores).
Lower test-SKU contention reportedly hid the issue.
Reported production SKUs: 64-128 core NUMA nodes.
Cache coherency invalidations (MESI storms)
Lock wait and cache traffic can grow sharply.
Cache-Line Bouncing & Starvation
Dozens of threads spinning on shared lock words
saturate inter-socket interconnect fabrics (UPI).
Reported symptom: CPU saturation as throughput fell.
Some queues may grow until requests time out.
Exact internal server counters are not public.
2. Confluence of Triggers (Nov 12)
Cascade Start
01:20 UTC: Teams Failover (15h Prior)
Microsoft Teams traffic shifted away from its
secondary gateway onto the primary gateway pool.
Cross-tenant blast radius: Exchange and Teams
now competed for the exact same gateway pool.
Baseline connection density rose sharply.
03:00 UTC: 14% Capacity Offline
Routine maintenance and prior-day upgrade tasks
took ~14% of gateway nodes out of active rotation.
Surviving 86% fleet absorbed full baseline load.
Utilization operating near the non-linear knee
of the M/M/c queuing latency curve (rho > 0.85).
16:20 UTC: NA Peak Ingress Surge
Morning business hours in Americas triggered
massive burst of MAPI, REST, and sync calls.
Lock contention triggered on first saturated nodes.
Node response latencies jumped from ms to 30s+.
Health check timeouts initiated global eviction.
3. Reported Fleet Eviction Cascade
Cascade
Health-Check Eviction Loop
Azure Front Door / L7 probes fail on slow nodes.
Load balancers remove them from active rotation.
Evicted capacity shifts arriving load onto survivors.
Survivors may then exceed their capacity.
Reportedly, more than 80% of gateway nodes were evicted.
Thundering-Herd Cold Restart Trap
Engineers rebooted frozen gateway instances.
Freshly booted nodes faced millions of clients
re-attempting TLS handshakes simultaneously.
Without warmed connection pools or caches,
Some nodes reportedly overloaded again after restart.
Aggressive Client Retry Amplification
Outlook desktop, web, iOS, Android, and third-party
clients retried while gateways were already saturated.
Retries added load to already saturated gateways.
Service disruption lasted about 23h 50m.
Bypass and staged ingress were part of reported recovery.
4. Engineering Recovery Architecture & Architectural Mitigations
Recovery & Traffic-Shedding Blueprint
1. Logic Bypass: Deployed emergency hotfix disabling July lock-contended code.
2. Decouple Gateways: Diverted Microsoft Teams traffic back to separate tier.
3. Edge Ingress Shedding: Azure Front Door rate-limited incoming connections
at edge PoPs to allow gateway nodes to initialize connection tables safely.
4. Phased Canary Ingress: Reintroduced traffic in controlled cohorts,
validating lock contention and queue depth telemetry at each increment.
5. Safe Cluster Reintegration: Nodes rejoined Anycast routing only after
sustaining stable TLS handshakes during the staged ingress ramp.
Global availability fully restored after 23 hours 50 minutes.
Architectural Mitigations & Concurrency Defenses
1. Hardware-Parity Staging: Mandate soak-testing on 64+ core SMP servers
to expose cache-line bouncing and Universal Scalability Law coherency stalls.
2. Partitioned Synchronization: Replace coarse mutexes with cache-padded
128 shards can reduce contention on the target hardware.
3. Decoupled Health Sampling: Cache status in atomic state.
BackgroundService updates it off the request path.
4. Non-Evicting Degradation: Signal edge proxies via x-envoy-degraded
or HTTP headers to shed traffic without removing nodes from Anycast pools.
Can reduce domino evictions during transient overload.
